extracted.intended_audience: federal agency staff, administrative law practitioners, hearing examiners, and policymakers involved in agency procedure and rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and statistical reporting standards for administrative proceedings before federal agencies, plus illustrative uniform rules (computation of time, presumptions, stipulations, form of decisions) and proposed admission/discipline procedures for attorneys practicing before agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purposes of the Office of Administrative Procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: With a view to achieving improvements in administrative procedures within the Executive departments and agencies of the Federal Government, the Office shall: (a) Carry on continuous studies of the adequacy of the procedures by which Federal departments and agencies determine the rights, duties, and privileges of persons; (b) Initiate cooperative effort among the departments and agencies and their respective bars to develop and adopt so far as practicable uniform rules of practice and procedure; (c) Collect and publish facts and statistics concerning the procedures of the departments and agencies; (d) Assist departments and agencies in the formulation and improvement of their administrative procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This statement is the Office's mandate and frames what counts as its evaluative and advisory activities; it implies prioritizing uniformity, data collection, study, and direct assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'proceeding' for reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'proceeding' means a matter which in normal course is referred to an examiner for evidentiary hearing, by oral or written presentation, and for recommended or initial decision by him, even though it may be a consolidated proceeding involving more than one petition, application, or complaint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Matters that involve joint hearings and a single binding decision are counted as one proceeding even if multiple dockets/claimants; the practical implication is aggregation when resolution is joint.

rubrics_metrics.name: When a proceeding is 'commenced' (counting commencement date)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the procedure contemplates hearing on filing (every petition/complaint), the proceeding is counted from the date of initial filing. Where hearing is not automatic and matters are subject to summary administrative grant or denial, the matter is counted as a proceeding only when it reaches the point where it is to be resolved by the hearing process (designation for hearing, entry upon hearing docket, or referral to office of hearing examiners).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This affects age and time-to-disposition statistics and must be applied consistently; different agencies' practices require careful mapping to these two models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Division into types of proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The division into types of proceedings employed in the tables is a division made by the reporting agencies, and characterizations have been abbreviated for the tables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comparisons across agencies should acknowledge that types are agency-defined and abbreviated; analysts should exercise caution when comparing types across agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table 1 metrics (backlog and volume columns)
rubrics_metrics.description: Table 1 columns: number of pending cases at beginning of fiscal year; new cases commenced during fiscal year; closed cases reopened during the year; cases closed during fiscal year; balance pending at the end of the fiscal year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these five measures (opening backlog, input, reopenings, output, closing backlog) to present overall volume/backlog. The report demonstrates use with agency and grand totals and notes distortion factors (e.g., Social Security influx).

rubrics_metrics.name: Age-of-proceeding grouping (Table 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Age of proceedings is measured from their commencement as described; age is demonstrated by age-grouping rather than averages or medians (e.g., <6 months, 6-12 months, 1-2 years, 2-3 years, >3 years).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grouping is preferred for indicating tendencies and boundaries; the report cites percentages in each age bracket and notes missing data for certain case types (e.g., Social Security, Indian probate).

rubrics_metrics.name: Manner of disposition categories (Table 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Disposition categories include: decided on the merits by agency final decision after examiner decision; decided by agencies without initial or recommended decision by an examiner; examiner's decision became final without agency review; dismissed or withdrawn without decision on merits; plus other dispositions such as default, consent, settlement, compromise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report gives counts and percentages for each category and emphasizes that a substantial share may be examiner decisions adopted as final. Analysts should separately track settlement/default categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall time from commencement to final agency disposition (Table 4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measures total elapsed time from commencement of proceeding to final agency disposition for matters decided on the merits after examiner decision; reported in time buckets (e.g., within 6 months, 6-12 months, 1-2 years, 2-3 years, >3 years).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to assess system timeliness; Social Security appeals to Appeals Council excluded for some computations. Percent distributions provided as benchmarks (e.g., 9% within 6 months, 42% 6-12 months, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Time from commencement to assignment to examiner (Table 5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measures period from commencement of proceeding to its assignment to an examiner, reported in buckets (assigned at commencement, within 1 month, 1-3 months, 3-6 months, 6-12 months, >1 year).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies agencies that assign immediately (FTC, SSA, Bureau of Indian Affairs, Office of Alien Property, Coast Guard) and quantifies proportions (e.g., 21% assigned at commencement among closed matters). Useful for diagnosing pre-examiner delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time under advisement by the agency (Table 6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measured from the date the matter was first ripe for agency final decision (last exceptions filed, record certified, etc.) to issuance of the agency's final decision; reported in time buckets with percentages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Data are not available for some appeals (e.g., Social Security cases taken to Appeals Council). Performance benchmarks given (e.g., 41% decided within 3 months; 9% took over a year).

rubrics_metrics.name: Part B scope: examiner-only period metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Part B covers only periods when a proceeding was in the hands of a hearing examiner, measuring from the date of assignment to the examiner to the date its pendency before him terminates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part B excludes stages before assignment and agency consideration after examiner decision (except where Table 12 expands scope). Enables comparison of examiner workload and speed over years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table 7: examiners' backlog and volume by fiscal year
rubrics_metrics.description: Gives number of proceedings pending before examiners at start and end of fiscal years, new cases assigned to examiners and reassigned/remanded, examiner output, and balance pending, enabling year-to-year comparison.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to compare examiner throughput between years; report notes effects of Social Security cases when interpreting totals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table 8: length of time proceedings had been pending before examiners
rubrics_metrics.description: For proceedings pending before examiners at year end, measures time from date of assignment to the examiner to the reference date (June 30), showing proportions over 1 year, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives trend comparison (e.g., 10.9% over a year in 1958 vs. 10.5% in 1957) and notes exceptions where data unavailable (Social Security, Indian probate).

rubrics_metrics.name: Table 9: manner of disposition by examiners
rubrics_metrics.description: Shows how pendency before hearing examiners was terminated (decided on merits after hearing, dismissed/withdrawn without decision, etc.) with counts and percentages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In 1958, 71.6% of examiner dispositions were on merits after hearing; 23% were dismissed/withdrawn, highlighting examiner decision predominance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table 10: total time in examiner's hands from assignment to decision
rubrics_metrics.description: Measures overall time an examiner handled a proceeding from assignment to the examiner to decision by the examiner, reported in buckets (e.g., disposed within 3 months, >2 years).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Benchmarks provided (1958: 53% disposed within 3 months; <1% >2 years); comparisons with prior year track changes in examiner timeliness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table 11: examiner time under advisement
rubrics_metrics.description: Measured from date of final submission to the examiner (last proposed findings/brief filed) to date examiner's decision issued; reported in buckets (≤1 month, ≤3 months, ≤6 months, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides timeliness benchmarks for deliberative phase (1958: 34% within 1 month, 84% within 3 months, 96% within 6 months).

rubrics_metrics.name: Table 12: hearing-examiner staffing and productivity metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes number of examiners employed, man-years of examiner time available (accounting for loans/separations), average number of days per man-year spent presiding over hearings and pre-hearing conferences, average number of decisions per man-year, and number of proceedings assigned for conduct of hearing only (no decision by examiner).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines counting rules (a 'day of hearing' counts whether full or part day, for one or multiple proceedings) and computes averages by dividing totals by man-years; caveat that the decisions-per-man-year column may include broader case types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computation of time (President's Conference illustrative rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: In computing any period of time prescribed or allowed by the (agency) rules, by order of the (agency) or by any applicable statute: exclude the day of the act/event/default that starts the period; include the last day unless it is Saturday, Sunday, or legal holiday (then extend to next business day); when period is less than 7 days, intermediate Saturdays, Sundays and holidays shall be excluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the recommended uniform computation rule agencies should adopt; it standardizes inclusion/exclusion of weekends and holidays, with special rule for short periods (<7 days).

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency rules for automatic extension when served by mail or for distant geography
rubrics_metrics.description: Some agency rules provide adding three days when service is by mail; one agency adds three days only when filing period following service by mail is ten days or less. Three agencies allow additional days for filing when parties reside in designated areas (typically five additional days), some allow twenty additional days for residents beyond continental U.S.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report identifies which agencies follow which add-days practices and recommends awareness of these variations when computing deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumptions (illustrative uniform rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency may make presumptions, with or without prior request or notice, upon proof of predicate facts 'without substantial dispute and by direct, clear, and convincing evidence.' Listed presumptions include: (i) Continuity, (ii) Identity, (iii) Delivery, (iv) Ordinary Course, (v) Acceptance of Benefit, (vi) Interference with Remedy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies evidentiary threshold and examples of presumptions agencies may adopt; must be consistent with surrounding facts and circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stipulations and admissions of record in multi-party proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Existence/non-existence of a material fact made in a stipulation or admission of record will be conclusively presumed against any party bound thereby, and no other evidence will be received for that party, provided: (i) it is binding upon parties making it, their privies, and other parties who do not expressly and unequivocally deny it upon service within five days; (ii) withdrawal prior to final decision may be permitted upon showing inadvertence or bona fide mistake and absence of unjust prejudice to others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets binding effect, service timetable (five days), and a narrow withdrawal standard to protect relying parties; intended to expedite multi-party proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and content required for every decision
rubrics_metrics.description: Every decision (recommended, initial, tentative, or final) shall contain, in order: (i) correct caption; (ii) description of nature and status of decision; (iii) separately identified headnotes of several points decided; (iv) designation of all parties and counsel; (v) concise statement of nature and background; (vi) concise statement of facts without recital of evidence; (vii) concise definition of issues; (viii) in separately identified paragraphs corresponding to headnotes, concise discussion of each issue, principles involved, determination with reasons and precedents; (ix) statement of rule, order, sanction or relief or denial thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a uniform structure for decisions to improve clarity, precedential value, and comparability across agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admission to practice before agencies (suggested uniform rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person who is a member in good standing of the bar of the Supreme Court of the United States or of the highest court of any state, territory, or the District of Columbia, and is not under any order suspending/enjoining/restraining/disbarring him in practice of law, may represent others before the agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule recommends dispensing with formal agency admission procedures in favor of uniform recognition of state/federal bar standing; notes adaptation needed where non-lawyers are admitted before particular agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature as certificate of authority
rubrics_metrics.description: When a person acting in a representative capacity appears in person or signs a paper, his appearance or signature shall constitute a representation to the agency that he is authorized and qualified to represent the particular party; further proof of authority may be required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treats signature/appearance as attestation to authority, simplifying verification while allowing the agency to request further proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service by or upon attorneys
rubrics_metrics.description: When a participant is represented by an attorney and that fact is made known in writing to the agency, any notice or other written communication required or permitted to be given to or by such participant shall be given to or by such attorney; if more than one attorney, service on any one is sufficient. If statute provides another service method, that must also be followed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures clarity in service and protects represented parties; agencies must still comply with statutory service requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for disqualification, suspension, or disbarment of attorneys
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency may disqualify, temporarily or permanently, any attorney who, after notice and hearing, does not meet admission requirements, has been disqualified/suspended/disbarred by another federal agency, is guilty of unethical or unprofessional conduct, or is not qualified to represent others before the agency. Contemptuous conduct at any hearing is ground for summary suspension without notice/opportunity for hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires notice and opportunity for hearing except for summary suspension for contemptuous conduct; agencies should adopt simple, adequate, and uniform discipline rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures for discipline of attorneys (complaint and hearing process)
rubrics_metrics.description: Complaint/discipline process: officer/employee reports alleged violation to General Counsel; General Counsel may investigate and either decline or initiate formal proceedings by filing a complaint served personally or by registered mail; respondent has ten days to answer (may not demur but may assert jurisdictional or scope objections and may request a hearing to be held within sixty days of request); default if no answer or appearance; General Counsel prosecutes at hearing; hearing before agency or panel, closed unless respondent requests open; respondent may be represented, call/cross-examine witnesses, and inspect record; record kept.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies timelines (10-day answer, 60-day hearing request), limits on pleading practice (no demurrer), process for default, and rights at hearing, providing a uniform disciplinary adjudication model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard of proof for attorney misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: In contested cases, charges must be established by a preponderance of the evidence; in cases where the respondent defaults, by prima facie evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets the evidentiary threshold for discipline findings and distinguishes between contested and default situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency orders, remedies, publication and notification after discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: After consideration, agency may order (1) disqualification temporarily or permanently from practice before it, or (2) dismiss charges. If disqualification ordered: (1) publish copy of order in the Federal Register; (2) send copy to appropriate state/territorial/D.C. authorities from which respondent derived license to practice; transcript of record available on payment; agency shall notify such authorities of termination of disqualification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures public record, inter-jurisdictional notification, and availability of the record for licensing authorities; remedies focused on practice before the agency rather than state licensure directly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggested uniform rule on discipline should include substantive and procedural provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: A suggested uniform rule on discipline of attorneys, which includes both substantive and procedural provisions, is included in the Appendix of this report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report recommends uniformity across agencies and provides model text (see Appendix) covering grounds, procedures, evidence, and publication—agencies are encouraged to adopt/adapt it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency rules on disbarment grounds (charted factors)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency rules on disbarment are charted across numerous potential grounds including: 'good cause,' violation of laws and regulations, unethical or unprofessional conduct, lacking required character or competence, misconduct in hearings, contemptuous or improper conduct, bribery, deception/misleading, and improper fees; the chart shows which agencies list which grounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the chart to compare scope of disciplinary bases across agencies; it demonstrates significant commonality as well as agency-specific differences.
